variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Start in A: with the hand empty in the initial execution scene, pick up the cube whose color is specified by the goal, pointing at its current visible center. For every subgoal, output the choice as the menu label alone, copied verbatim (such as "A", "B", or "C"); never append the action description. Supply the target separately as a [y, x] point for options requiring one. Determine the current grasp state from the entire currently shown execution interval, not the demonstration's final hand pose or the final execution observation alone. Apply this assessment before any empty-hand or retry-A rule. Descent onto the goal cube, closure to a cube-sized opening (about 46%), and withdrawal with that opening maintained establishes a completed pickup unless later execution observations show an actual release or clear grasp failure. An explicit held annotation anywhere in the interval also establishes possession unless subsequent observations show release or clear failure. A missing final held label, a cube center near its former tabletop position, or disagreement between the reported cube center and wrist position does not by itself establish failure or an empty hand. When pickup completion is established and not subsequently invalidated, choose B using selected_target as specified below; do not repeat A. For B, point at the target matching selected_target, using its current visible center when available and the stored point if occluded. Do not select another target based on proximity to the held cube. Choose retry A at the available goal cube only on positive evidence of grasp failure, such as visibly closing on nothing, and only if no later observation in the current execution interval establishes successful possession. Do not infer failure merely from an omitted held label or an inconsistent reported cube position. After a successful release onto the selected target, the goal is complete; no button press is required. C is not used for these goals: button presses in the demonstration neither reset the placement count nor require imitation. If an unexpected decision follows a completed correct placement and a menu command is mandatory, choose A on the goal cube and subsequently B onto the same selected target, rather than pressing the button. For other uncovered situations, use B when holding the goal cube and selected_target is known. Use the empty-hand fallback A only when the hand is empty and the goal cube can be located, after checking the whole current execution interval: an established pickup blocks this fallback unless a subsequent actual release or clear grasp failure is observed. The cube's being locatable does not establish an empty hand. Retain the completed-correct-placement rule above when a release has completed the goal. If selected_target is unknown and a drop is mandatory, use the nearest visible target as a deterministic fallback, without claiming it is the demonstrated target.

fields.name: selected_target
fields.description: When the incoming memory is empty and the current step includes the demonstration, read the cube color and placement ordinal from the goal. Initialize in two stages. First build a temporary chronological list of the goal-colored cube's completed releases onto targets: a carried cube is lowered onto a target, released, and left there as the hand withdraws. Record each release once with the physical target receiving it. Do not count initial positions, flyovers, button presses, or releases onto unmarked workspace; button presses do not reset the count. Select the requested ordinal entry using one-based counting, checking the releases through that entry to ensure that it is the requested placement rather than the preceding one. Second, follow the physical target identified at that entry through every remaining demonstration observation into the first execution scene. Keep the release list temporary, not in persistent memory. Maintain temporary identities for all targets while scanning the remaining demonstration; treat target lists as unordered detections, not persistent identity indices. Track continuous motion through temporary occlusion, small shifts, large movements, and exchanges of positions. For each interval of coordinated movement, associate all targets jointly across the entire interval using successive displacement directions and smooth path continuation. First identify targets supported as stationary throughout the interval, allowing small visible-center wobble, and reserve their detections for those identities. Determine stationarity from intermediate observations throughout the interval, not merely matching start and end positions. Then associate the remaining moving branches jointly, allowing curved paths; do not jump from a moving branch onto a nearby stationary target merely because that assignment is shorter. Use intermediate observations to resolve correspondences rather than independently assigning each identity to the nearest detection at each frame. When targets pass on different sides of their shared midpoint, follow each identity along its own intermediate branch to its endpoint. Do not restore identities from the final layout or match the original release coordinate directly to the nearest execution target: a return to the same set of positions does not establish that each physical target returned to its own position. Distinguish coherent movement across observations from small apparent center shifts caused by occlusion. Before writing, verify separately that the release-list entry has the requested ordinal and that its physical target's tracked endpoint matches the chosen target in the first execution scene. If no coherent target movement occurs after the selected release, preserve that target's identity through occlusion-related center shifts rather than substituting an earlier placement's target. Resolve the selected target's endpoint against the first execution scene, then discard the temporary release list and tracks after writing its canonical center. Target movement does not change the placement ordinal. Write the selected physical target's center in the first execution scene as [y, x]; do not store intermediate trajectories. On subsequent steps copy the incoming selected_target unchanged, regardless of the current grasp or target-center wobble. If the demonstration and first execution scene do not establish the requested placement or the selected physical target's identity, write "unknown" rather than inventing a placement or a target correspondence. e.g. [116, 163]
fields.annotation: Store one [y, x] point identifying the target on which the goal-named cube was placed at the goal-requested ordinal during the demonstration. Count completed placements onto targets chronologically, not frames, initial cube positions, flyovers, button presses, or the final release onto the unmarked central workspace. Identify a placement by lowering the carried cube onto a target and releasing it. Identify the physical target at the requested completed release, then follow its identity through the remainder of the demonstration into the first execution scene, including occlusion, large movements, and exchanges of positions with other targets. Use continuous trajectories and the motion of all targets to resolve identity, not proximity to the original release location or the final layout alone. Target movement does not change the placement ordinal. Store that physical target's center in the first execution scene as the canonical [y, x] point. If the requested placement or the selected target's identity cannot be established from the demonstration and first execution scene, write "unknown". Write this point at decision step #1 and retain it unchanged at every subsequent decision step.  e.g. [116, 163]

history.critique:
field selected_target, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  The failures occurred when a goal requested an ordinal placement and, after the cube was returned to the central workspace, demonstration targets moved and exchanged positions. The policy correctly chose to pick up the goal-colored cube, but stored the execution target nearest the original placement location. The annotations instead identified the moved target: for example, the first green-cube placement was on the lower target, which subsequently moved to [101, 166]. This breaks PREDICTABILITY because the existing rule mentions only occlusion and small coordinate shifts, not genuine target motion. Retain one field containing the first execution scene's center of the physical target selected by the requested chronological placement. Identify that target at the completed release, then follow its identity through the remainder of the demonstration, including large movements and exchanges of positions. Count releases exactly as before; target movement does not change the placement ordinal. Write the final matched execution-scene point at the first decision and retain it unchanged thereafter. For example, write [101, 166] for a selected lower target whose demonstrated motion ends at the image-right target. Remove the episode-specific lookup values and replace the small-shift-only identity guidance with this full-motion tracking rule.

field selected_target, POLICY PROMPT
  When the demonstration showed targets exchanging positions after the cube's placements, the policy chose the correct pickup but mapped the requested release location directly to the nearest target in the initial execution scene. Consequently its stored point differed from the annotated destination of the moving physical target. This is a PREDICTABILITY failure, not evidence that placement counting should change. With empty incoming memory and the demonstration visible, count completed target releases of the goal-colored cube chronologically and select the requested one. Then continue scanning every remaining demonstration observation to track that target's motion until execution begins. Associate successive target observations using continuous trajectories, accounting jointly for the other targets rather than independently matching the original placement coordinate to the final layout. Targets can exchange locations even when the final layout resembles the original layout. For example, a selected target can move from approximately [137, 104] through [115, 110] and [98, 135] to the image-right target, whose execution center is [101, 166]. Likewise, an upper target can move to the lower position, and an image-right target can move to the image-left position. Store only the selected target's execution-scene center, not these intermediate trajectories; all tracking occurs within the demonstration available at the first decision. On later decisions copy selected_target unchanged. Preserve the existing release-count exclusions and unknown handling when identity genuinely cannot be established.

The policy repeated A even though selected_target correctly identified the requested target. This is a subgoal-selection failure, not missing historical information: the existing policy prompt already provides sufficient evidence for B, but its fallback to A when the cube can be located was apparently applied ahead of its pickup-completion rule. Make that precedence explicit. Before applying any empty-hand or retry fallback, examine the entire currently shown execution interval.
